LESSON: GOOD CITIZENSHIP IN SCHOOL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya
Topic 5.1: Good Citizenship in School
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Good Citizenship in School, part of Citizenship and Governance in Kenya in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How can we demonstrate good citizenship in school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Good Citizenship in School together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: Learners make observations as they undertake group activities and exchange new ideas while designing a

poster with qualities of a good citizen in school.

● Citizenship: Learners develop information and communication skills as they engage a resource person to discuss the importance of

good citizenship.

Values:
● Unity: Learners design a poster with qualities of a good citizen in school.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Honesty: Learners speaks and acts honestly as they discuss in groups how to become a good citizen in school.

● Social cohesion: Learners develop harmonious coexistence as they discuss in groups how to become a good citizen in school.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● Religious Education as learners use digital, braille or print resources to identify qualities of a good citizen in school.

● English, Kiswahili and KSL as learners write an essay on a good digital citizen (using technology in a positive way) and share the

essays in class.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Vetted digital resources with assistive technology, braille resources, manilla papers, crayons, wet paints and braille cards.
